items.text: A celebrity party, where attendees, including a rapper wearing only a sock, sparked an official backlash in Russia amid the ongoing war with Ukraine and a conservative social agenda. The rapper received a 15-day jail term, sponsors severed contracts, and even President Putin expressed discontent. The event termed ‘almost naked’ triggered swift condemnation from authorities, soldiers in Ukraine, and Putin himself. High-profile figures, associated with state TV entertainment, faced severe consequences, including contract cancellations and legal actions. Blogger Anastasia Ivleeva, the party organizer, apologized twice after displaying a valuable chain, facing a tax investigation and a lawsuit for moral suffering. The scandal coincides with Putin’s emphasis on social conservatism, encouraging larger families and restricting LGBT activists. The incident outraged those supporting the war, leading to public condemnation and calls for accountability. Difficult words: backlash (a strong negative reaction), severe (ended abruptly), condemnation (expressing very strong disapproval). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Russia, there was a big problem with a controversial party where people wore very few clothes. A rapper got in trouble and went to jail for 15 days. Companies stopped contracts with famous people who were at the party. Even President Putin didn’t like the event. The party happened during the war in Ukraine, and many people thought it was wrong. The person who organized the party said sorry two times. Now, she has problems with taxes and might have to pay a lot of money. Some people say the party was bad because soldiers are fighting, and it is a tough time. It is not appropriate to party like this. People are angry, and they want those who did the party to be punished . Difficult words: controversial (something what people talk and argue about a lot), contract (a formal agreement between two or more people or organizations), punished (when someone gets a penalty for doing something wrong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a big party in Russia. Famous people are at the party. They wear very few clothes. This creates problems. A rapper goes to jail for 15 days. He wears only a sock. Companies stop working with famous people. Even President Putin does not like it. The party happens during the war in Ukraine. Many people do not think that partying is right. A woman organizes the party. Now, she is in trouble with taxes . She may have to pay a lot of money. Some people say that the party is bad because soldiers are fighting. It is a hard time for many people. Difficult words: partying (going to a party and having fun), organize (to plan an event), tax (money which people and companies pay to the state). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the United States, hospitals are increasingly suing patients over unpaid bills. This phenomenon, escalating since the 80s and 90s, involves lawyers pursuing debtors on behalf of medical providers. The consequences for patients unable to pay include court proceedings, wage garnishment , and home foreclosure. While a comprehensive national overview is challenging due to the lack of centralized tracking, Wisconsin stands out with tens of thousands of such cases. Maryland, however, has successfully curtailed this practice through new legislation which resulted in zero cases in 2023. Medical professionals express shame, and awareness among healthcare providers may contribute to ending this detrimental practice. Despite some positive developments since 2019, with fewer cases reported, the damaging impact on patients remains significant. Difficult words: garnishment (taking money from a person’s wages as a result of a court order), curtail (to reduce or restrict), detrimental (harmful or damaging). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Some US patients don’t pay hospital bills and hospitals are suing them. This trend started in the 80s. Lawyers pursue debtors on behalf of medical providers. As a result, patients face court proceedings, wage garnishment , and even taking properties . Wisconsin stands out with tens of thousands of cases. On the other hand, Maryland changed legislation and there were no cases in 2023. Healthcare providers are upset about the situation. There were some good changes since 2019, with fewer cases reported, but many patients are still having big money problems. Difficult words: sue (to take legal action against someone), wage garnishment (taking money from someone’s wages to pay a debt), property (a thing which belongs to someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some patients in the US do not pay hospital bills. Hospitals are suing these people. This means that people who cannot pay may go to court. They may lose money from their paychecks . They may even lose their homes. Very many cases happen in Wisconsin. Maryland makes new laws , and in 2023, there are no cases. Doctors and nurses find out that their hospital sues patients. They feel very bad about it. This is not good for patients and hospitals. Since 2019, some places have fewer cases. Laws are changing. It is good news for people with medical debt . Difficult words: paycheck (a check for money which you get for your work), law (rules of a country), debt (money which you have to give back to someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Shanghai’s well-known landmarks vanished behind dense fog during the year-end holiday, causing concerns about potential transport disruptions . The weather bureau issued a red warning for fog that spans from Hab province in the north to Shanghai in the south and lasts over 24 hours. This marked Shanghai’s first red fog warning since 2017. Residents were surprised by the obscured cityscape, with key structures like the Shanghai Center Tower and Oriental Pearl Tower becoming barely visible. The fog led to the temporary suspension of city ferries, highway sections, and a bridge to a container port. Widespread flight delays occurred, exceeding 600 flights in various cities. The severe weather, attributed to high humidity and poor atmospheric diffusion , was expected to improve as a cold wave swept across China, concluding a year marked by climate extremes, including cold snaps , scorching heat, and intense storms. Difficult words: disruption (disturbance or problems), atmospheric diffusion (spreading of pollutants in the air), cold snap (a period of very cold weather). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Shanghai faced a thick fog during the year-end holiday, which caused worry about transport problems. Authorities issued a red fog warning which covered areas from the north in Hab province to Shanghai in the south. It was the first warning since 2017. Famous landmarks like the Shanghai Center Tower and Oriental Pearl Tower became almost invisible , which surprised residents. Ferries, highways, and bridges temporarily closed due to the fog. Over 600 flights faced delays in many cities. Experts expect that the bad weather will improve with a coming cold wave. China endured extreme weather throughout the year, from periods of very cold weather to heatwaves and big storms. Difficult words: landmark (a building or structure which you can easily see), invisible (something what you can’t see), temporarily (for some time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Shanghai has a thick fog during the holiday. It is hard to see famous places. The fog covers a large area, from the north to the south. Authorities warn about the fog. This is the first warning since 2017. People in Shanghai are surprised. They cannot see the tall buildings like the Shanghai Center Tower and Oriental Pearl Tower. Ferries , highways , and a bridge must close for some time. Over 600 flights are late in different cities. Experts think that the weather will get better with a cold wind. This year, China has strange weather, from very cold times to very hot days and heavy rain in Beijing and other places. Difficult words: fog (air which is hard to see through), ferry (a big ship which carries people, cars, and other things), highway (a fast road). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ukraine launched a cruise missile attack on a large Russian landing warship in Crimea, damaging the vessel and killing at least one person. The Novocherkassk ship, crucial for potential Russian operations along the Black Sea coast, was targeted in the port of Feodosia. The Russian defense ministry confirmed the attack and suggested the ship might struggle to re-enter service. Both nations have been engaged in conflict since Russia’s annexation of Crimea in 2014. Ukraine, using air-launched cruise missiles, inflicted significant damage, hindering Russian attempts to expand its territorial control. The incident underscores the ongoing tensions between the two countries, with Ukraine successfully launching attacks on key Russian assets in Crimea. Difficult words: inflict (to cause someone or something to experience something unpleasant), hinder (to make something difficult happen), underscore (to emphasize the importance of). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ukraine attacked a big Russian ship in Crimea, the attack happened at night. The ship named Novocherkassk was in the port of Fedosia. It got badly damaged, and at least one person died. Russian officials confirmed the attack and said that the ship might not be able to operate anymore. Russia and Ukraine are in a fight since 2014 when Russia annexed Crimea. Ukraine wants to stop Russia from taking more territories near the Black Sea. The country is trying to attack important Russian assets in Crimea and to reduce Russia’s power in the area. Difficult words: operate (to work), annex (to take a territory of another country), asset (something what belongs to a person, company, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ukraine attacks a big Russian ship in Crimea. They use rockets at night. The ship gets hit. At least one person dies. Russian officials say that the ship may not work well again. Russia does not say much about the attack. But it is a big problem for Russia. Russia and Ukraine are fighting since 2014. In 2014, Russia takes Crimea by force . Now, Crimea is part of Russia. Ukraine does not want Russia to be so strong in the Black Sea. There are more attacks. Ukraine damages Russia’s ships and other things. Difficult words: by force (when you use power to get something), damage (to hurt). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Serbian police have detained 38 people involved in protests against the results of the December 17 elections, which international monitors deemed unfair. The opposition group Serbia Against Violence has been protesting election fraud allegations , particularly in Belgrade. The governing populists were declared winners, leading to ongoing demonstrations. In one instance, protesters attempted to enter Belgrade city hall, resulting in clashes with riot police using teargas and batons. The opposition refuses to recognize the election results, urging the EU to investigate and calling for a new, fair election. US Ambassador Christopher Hill denounced violence during the protests, emphasizing the importance of transparent and democratic processes. The Serbian president accused the west of encouraging opposition protests, with Russia supporting the government. Difficult words: allegation (clam without proof), populist (a politician who wants to get the support of ordinary people by giving them what they want), denounce (to publicly criticize). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Serbian police arrested 38 people who protested against the results of the December 17 elections. The opposition group claimed that the elections were not fair, especially in Belgrade. Police clashed with protesters who tried to enter city hall. The opposition doesn’t accept the result of the election, and they ask the EU to investigate and a new fair election. US Ambassador didn’t agree with the violence, and he said that elections had to be democratic and transparent. The Serbian president accused the west of supporting the protests. But international observers said that there were some troubles, such as buying votes and media bias . Difficult words: opposition (people with different ideas and opinions than the main political party), accuse (to say that someone did something wrong), bias (to act in favor of or against an idea or thing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Serbian police arrest 38 people. These people protest against the election results on December 17. Some protesters try to get into the city hall. Some people believe that the election is not fair. Some problems are in Belgrade. Some politicians are not happy with the results either. They ask the EU for help. They want a new and fair election. The Serbian president thinks that western countries help the protesters. Russia supports the government, too. Some people say that the election had problems, like buying votes and unfair media . Difficult words: election (when people vote a person for a job in politics), support (to help), media (TV, radio and internet). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A potential merger between Warner Brothers Discovery and Paramount Global, two major entertainment conglomerates , is being discussed. The CEOs of both companies, David Zaslav and Bob Bakish, recently met in Manhattan to explore the possibility. The merger would create a massive media entity , combining assets like Warner Brothers Studios and Paramount Plus streaming service. While business advantages are evident , questions remain about the details and which company would absorb the other. Federal regulators might play a role, and the likelihood of the merger passing is uncertain, given the challenges faced by major mergers in the current business landscape. Difficult words: conglomerate (a large corporation formed by the merging of different companies), entity (a thing with independent existence), evident (clear). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Warner Brothers Discovery and Paramount Global are considering a merger , a recent report says. The CEOs David Zaslav and Bob Bakish met in Manhattan to discuss the possible merger of the two entertainment giants . This merger would result in a big media conglomerate , which would bring together assets such as Warner Brothers Studios and the Paramount Plus streaming service. While both companies face troubles in the changing world of media, officials may have an impact on the result of the merger. The chances of the merger are not too high. There were some mergers in the industry recently which didn’t turn out very well. Difficult words: merger (two companies getting together), giant (a very large company), conglomerate (a large company formed by a merger). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two big companies Warner Brothers Discovery and Paramount Global may merge. When two companies merge, they join together to make one big company. The CEOs talk about it in Manhattan. They talk about making a very big media company. They have lots of movies and TV shows. The bosses meet to decide. But we do not know who will be the boss of the new company. It may be hard. Some people may not like it. There are official rules . They can have an impact on the merger . Both companies have good things. Warner Brothers has its studios. Paramount has a streaming service called Paramount Plus. We have to wait and see if they can join. Difficult words: CEO (the boss of a company), rule (what someone must or must not do), merger (when two companies join together). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Alexei Navalny, a prominent Russian opposition figure, has been located in the IK-3 penal colony , known as the Polar Wolf prison, situated north of the Arctic Circle in the Yamal-Nenets region. Navalny’s lawyer visited him on Monday, and while his spokeswoman assures that he is alright, concerns arise about the harsh conditions and isolation imposed on him. The prison is part of the former Soviet GULAG system and is notorious for its severe regime and extreme climate, with temperatures dropping to minus 28 degrees Celsius. Navalny’s allies express worry about his well-being, emphasizing the Russian authorities’ attempts to isolate him. The US State Department calls for his immediate release, condemning his detention as unjust and expressing deep concern for his welfare. Difficult words: prominent (important or well known), penal colony (a place in a remote location where prisoners are sent to live), notorious (famous or well known, typically for some bad quality). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Alexei Navalny is a Russian opposition leader who is now in the so-called Polar Wolf prison, The prison is situated north of the Arctic Circle. His lawyer visited him recently, and he worried about Navalny’s well-being . The prison’s hard conditions and isolation worry people. Temperatures can drop to minus 28 degrees Celsius there. Navalny’s allies believe that officials keep him away ahead of the March presidential election. US officials worry about Navaly’s health and they ask Russia to release him. Navalny is in prison for political reasons, but he keeps saying that he did nothing wrong. Last month, he spoke about the bad situation in Russian prisons, including poor dental care. Difficult words: opposition (a group of people in politics who have different ideas and opinions), well-being (being healthy and happy), ally (a person or organization that helps another in an activity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Alexei Navalny is a leader of the opposition in Russia. It means that he speaks strongly against the government. Navalny is in prison for some time. His lawyer visits him. He says that Navalny is in a prison called the Polar Wolf. This is a place far away from Moscow. It is north of the Arctic Circle . It can be very cold there, about minus 28 degrees Celsius. The regime is very hard there. Some people worry about Navalny’s safety and health. The US wants him free. Some people say that Navalny is away because people in Russia will vote for a new president in March. Navalny says that he does nothing wrong. He says that the situation in Russian prisons is very bad. Difficult words: Arctic Circle (a line around the northern part of the world), regime (a system of doing things), safety (when someone is safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A sprinting ostrich shocked motorists and took the Internet by storm as it ran down a federal highway in Malaysia. People could see the female bird in the right lane of the highway, leading traffic behind her. Local news outlets said that the ostrich named Chickaboo escaped from her owner Darren Chow when he was driving her to the Ostrich Wonderland’s farm in Semenyih. The owner, an animal trainer, decided to take the ostrich back to the farm where she had been originally born because she was too big for him to keep. The driver who filmed the video said that he had visited the ostrich in her new home, and she was safe and doing well. Difficult words: sprint (run quickly), take something by storm (have great success). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Malaysia, an ostrich ran down a highway. Its owner was driving it to an ostrich farm when it escaped . The man was taking it to the farm, where the ostrich was born because it became too big for him to keep. A man on the highway filmed a video of the ostrich and said that he visited the ostrich. It is safe and doing well. Difficult words: ostrich (a big bird, which cannot fly, but runs very fast), escape (break free from a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Malaysia. A man has an ostrich . He cannot keep it. It gets too big for him. He is taking it to a farm. The man and the ostrich are on a highway. The ostrich escapes . Another man films the ostrich. In the end, the ostrich gets to the farm. It is safe. It is doing well. Difficult words: ostrich (a big bird that cannot fly but runs very fast), escape (break free/get out from a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

New regulations in China aim to curb spending on video games, leading to a substantial market value decline for major gaming companies like Tencent and NetEase. The rules, introduced by regulators, prevent online games from providing rewards for daily logins, initial spending, or consecutive spending sessions. This impacted common incentive mechanisms in the gaming industry. Investors reacted with concern, causing nearly 80 billion dollars in market value losses. Tencent Games’ vice president Vigo Zhang reassured that the company’s business model wouldn’t require fundamental changes, emphasizing adherence to regulatory requirements. The regulations also include stipulations on setting spending limits and storage of user data within China. Despite investor concerns, the industry may find relief in the proposed faster game approval process. Difficult words: incentive (a thing that motivates and encourages someone to do something), adherence (following a rule), stipulation (specific requirement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

China made new rules to control how much people spend on video games. The rules caused big problems for top gaming companies like Tencent and NetEase. The rules say that online games can’t give rewards for logging in every day or spending money for the first time. This worried investors and the companies lost nearly 80 billion dollars. Tencent’s vice president said they don’t need big changes and follow the rules. The rules also say games must limit how much players can spend. Some parts of the rules might help the game industry by making the approval process faster. Difficult words: log in (to enter a game), investor (a person who puts money in a business), approval (the process of agreeing with something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China makes new rules for video games. These rules stop people from spending too much money. Big game companies like Tencent and NetEase lose a lot of money because of these rules. The rules say that games cannot give gifts for logging in or spending money. Investors worry. The companies lose almost 80 billion dollars. Tencent is one of the big companies. They do not need to change a lot and they follow the rules. The rules also say that games can only let players spend some amount of money. Some rules may help the game industry. It will be easier to approve new games. Difficult words: log in (to enter a game), investor (a person who puts money in a business), approve (to agree with something or make it officially possible). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A dog in Peru found itself stranded in a canal in Trujillo, a city in north western Peru, but luckily, police officers were on hand to help the dog out. One of them stripped down to his underwear and got into the water to help the drowning animal. He eventually grabbed the dog and handed it to the first in line of the human chain that people formed along the canal bank. People saved the dog, and it looked only a little shaken up by the ordeal . Difficult words: stranded (lost, unable to get out from somewhere), strip down (remove all clothing), grab (take quickly), the first in line (the first person or thing in the front of the line), human chain (when people hold hands to form a ‘chain’), ordeal (something very bad that happens to you). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Peru, a dog found itself in a canal and it could not get out. Luckily, police officers were on hand to help it out. One officer even stripped down to his underwear and got into the water to help the drowning animal. He grabbed the dog and passed him to another officer. They saved the dog and he was only a little shaken. Difficult words: drown (when you are in the water and you are dying because of it), grab (take). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This happens in Peru. A dog gets into the canal . It cannot get out. It is in danger. Luckily, there are police officers nearby . They help the dog. One police officer gets undressed. He jumps into the water. He picks up the dog. He passes it to another officer. They save the dog. He is only a little shaken . Difficult words: canal (a river which people build for boats), nearby (near, close, not far), shaken (shocked). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A tragic incident occurred at Charles University in Prague, the Czech Republic, where a student shot and killed 14 people and injured 25 others before being found dead. The police chief described it as a premeditated violent attack inspired by similar incidents abroad. The shooter’s father was also found dead earlier in the day. The shooter, previously unknown to the police, had a significant arsenal . Investigations revealed his connection to a recent double murder. The prime minister canceled his trip, and European leaders sent condolences. The country mourns with flags at half-mast , religious services, and a minute of silence. The incident is the deadliest in the country since 1993. Gun crime is relatively rare in the Czech Republic. In December 2019, a 42-year-old gunman killed six people at a hospital waiting room in the eastern city of Ostrava, while in 2015 a 63-year-old man shot seven men and a woman dead in the south-eastern town of Uhersky Brod. Difficult words: premeditated (planned in advance), arsenal (a collection of weapons and military equipment), half-mast (a flag that has been brought down to a point halfway down the pole as an expression of sadness at someone’s death). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A tragic event unfolded at Charles University in Prague, the Czech Republic. A 24-year-old student carried out a planned attack in which he killed 14 and injured 25 people. Earlier on the same day, police found dead the shooter’s father. It seems that the incident was inspired by similar events abroad. On 23 December, flags flew at half-mast as the country mourned the victims. The shooter was unknown to the police, but he had several weapons, and a few days before the attack, he killed two other people, a man and a two-month-old baby. Such attacks are not very common in the country. The incident was the deadliest since 1993. Difficult words: unfold (to develop), half-mast (when a flag is halfway down because someone died), mourn (to feel very sad because someone died). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A terrible attack happens at Charles University in Prague, the Czech Republic. A man kills several people. The man is only 24 years old. He is a student at the university. The student plans the attack. He has more guns with him. He kills 14 people and hurts 25 people. Earlier in the day, he kills his father. Then, he travels to Prague by bus. The man kills himself before the police do it. Police find out that the man kills two more people a few days earlier. He kills a man and a two-month-old baby. On December 23, the country mourns . Such attacks are not usual in the country. This is the worst attack since 1993. Difficult words: terrible (very bad), mourn (to be very sad because someone is dead). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A woman in Alabama, the United States, with a rare condition resulting in two uteri , recently gave birth to healthy twin girls. Kelsey Hatcher and her husband Caleb welcomed Roxi Layla and Rebel Laken at the University of Alabama at Birmingham Hospital. The unique pregnancy, termed dicavitary, had a one-in-a-million chance of occurring. Hatcher’s obstetrician expressed surprise at the rare scenario. The high-risk pregnancy led to induction at 39 weeks, culminating in a 20-hour labor resulting in both babies being born, one vaginally and the other via C-section. Although typically twins share one uterus, the medical team labeled them as fraternal twins. Hatcher looks forward to sharing the complete birth story while cherishing family time during the holidays. Difficult words: uterus (womb), obstetrician (a doctor who specializes in delivering babies and caring for women during pregnancy), induction (bringing on the birth, typically by the use of drugs). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Alabama, the United States, a woman with a rare condition successfully gave birth to twin girls. The woman has two wombs . Kelsey Hatcher and her husband welcomed their daughters Roxi Layla and Rebel Laken at the University of Alabama at Birmingham Hospital. Kelsey had a one-in-a-million chance that she would have such a condition. Even her doctor was surprised. Doctors ended the high-risk pregnancy at 39 weeks, after a 20-hour labor . One girl was born naturally and the other via C-section . Kelsey plans to share the full birth story soon, but now, she is happy to be home to bond and recover during the holidays. Difficult words: womb (the organ in which a baby develops), labor (giving birth), C-section (when a surgeon cuts the mother’s belly to take out a baby). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Alabama, the United States, a woman with two wombs gives birth to twin girls. Kelsey Hatcher and her husband welcome Roxi Layla and Rebel Laken at a hospital. This pregnancy is very unusual. The chance is one in a million. Hatcher’s doctor knows about it. But he is very surprised. The pregnancy is risky . Doctors end it at 39 weeks. After 20 hours, the twins are born—one normally and the other through an operation. Usually, twins share one womb. Hatcher is excited to share the full story and is now at home. She is enjoying her daughters and the holidays. Difficult words: womb (an organ in a woman’s body where a baby grows), pregnancy (when a woman has a baby inside her body), risky (dangerous). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

With over 40% of American adults being obese, the promising market for new weight-loss drugs is attracting attention. Analyst Rob Cyran warns that while drugs like Nova nordis SPI and Eli zip bound may revolutionize obesity treatment, their harsh side effects and high costs could slow widespread adoption. Currently, only a small percentage of the 100 million obese Americans are expected to use these drugs by the start of 2024. The expensive monthly cost, exceeding 1,000 dollars without insurance, and tightening reimbursement policies from companies and governments may impede their growth. Despite potential challenges, investors remain optimistic, affecting various industries like packaged food, fast-food restaurants, and medical firms catering to obesity-related diseases. Difficult words: revolutionize (to change something radically), reimbursement (repayment for expenses), impede (to delay or prevent by obstructing something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Investors are optimistic about new weight-loss drugs, such as Nova nordis SPI and Eli zip bound, which should treat obesity effectively. More than 40% of Americans are obese, but these drugs cost more than 1,000 dollars per month without insurance, and possible side effects may stop people from using them. Analysts predict that by the beginning of 2024, only a few of the 100 million obese Americans will use these therapies . Companies and governments are not willing to pay for these drugs, which has an impact, too. Although there are problems in the industry, packaged food, and medical firms are already experiencing stock decrease. Difficult words: side effect (a secondary effect of a drug, usually a negative one), therapy (the way of dealing with a health problem), packaged food (food which people pack and sell). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More than 40% of Americans are obese . That is 100 million people. Companies make drugs to help these people. New drugs are for example Nova nordis SPI and Eli zip bound. Scientists are excited about them. But these drugs are very expensive. They cost more than 1,000 a month. They have side effects. It means that patients can have some other problems when whey take these drugs. Not too many people will probably buy these drugs. Companies and governments do not want to pay for these drugs. The market is changing. Some medical firms are having problems. When people are healthy, they do not have business. Difficult words: obese (very fat), excited (happy), patient (a sick person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In a historic decision approved by Pope Francis, the Vatican announced that Roman Catholic priests can now give blessings to same-sex couples. This landmark ruling overturned a 2021 declaration, and it allows priests to perform blessings as long as they aren’t part of regular Church rituals. The Vatican emphasizes that such blessings don’t legitimize irregular situations but symbolize God’s acceptance of all individuals. It explicitly distinguishes these blessings from the sacrament of heterosexual marriage. Priests are granted discretion on a case-by-case basis to support individuals seeking God’s help through a simple blessing. While the Church maintains that same-sex attraction is not sinful, it acknowledges that homosexual acts are. The move has been praised by advocates for LGBT rights in the Church but is likely to face opposition from conservatives, raising concerns about potential schisms . Difficult words: explicitly (in a clear and detailed manner), sacrament (an important religious ceremony in the Christian Church), schism (a division or conflict within an organization). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Vatican will allow Roman Catholic priests to offer blessings to same-sex couples. Pope Francis approved this. Priests can perform blessings, but these blessings must not be part of regular Church rituals. The Vatican says that these blessings do not validate unusual situations but they show that God accepts all people. Priests can give blessings to individuals who need God’s help. The Church states that same-sex attraction is not a sin but homosexual acts are. People from the LGBT community welcome the change but they are afraid of some problems within the Church. Difficult words: blessing (a special wish or favor from God), validate (to make something officially acceptable), sin (something what you do and it breaks the laws of God). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from the Vatican. Pope Francis says yes to a new rule. This rule says that priests in the Catholic Church can give blessings to same-sex couples. This is a big change. It shows that God welcomes everyone. The rule says priests can decide to bless anyone who asks for God’s help. But it is not the same as getting married. The Church says that it is okay when a woman likes another woman or when a man likes another man. But some things are wrong. Some people are happy about this change. Others think that it may bring problems to the Church. The new rule says the blessing should not look like a usual wedding . It can happen in different places. Difficult words: priest (a religious leader in the Christian Church), blessing (God’s help), wedding (a ceremony in which two people marry). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

British teenager Alex Batty, allegedly kidnapped six years ago, escaped across the Pyrenees when his mother planned to move to Finland. Living a nomadic lifestyle with his mother and solar-enthusiast grandfather, Alex, now 17, survived on whatever he found in fields during his journey. Spending two years in spiritual communities across Spain, Morocco, and France, he decided to flee when his mother announced the move to Finland. With only 100 euros and a skateboard, he revealed his desperation to a passing driver, expressing the need for a future. Found in a remote corner of France, Alex is expected to reunite with his grandmother who is his legal guardian. His mother, Melanie Batty, remains missing, possibly in Finland. Despite his years away, Alex appears calm and intelligent, sharing details of his nomadic life. French prosecutors are investigating while ensuring the safe return of the boy, who is set to return to the UK accompanied by British police officers. British teenager Alex Batty allegedly escaped his mother’s custody six years ago and traveled across the Pyrenees when she announced her plans to move to Finland. Alex, now 17, lived a nomadic lifestyle with his grandfather and mother, and he spent two years in spiritual communities across Spain, Morocco, and France. His breaking point came when his mother said that she wanted to move to Finland. Carrying only 100 euros and a skateboard, he met a driver in a remote place in France. Alex told the driver that he needed a future. Alex will reunite with his legal guardian, grandmother Susan. Authorities don’t know where Alex’s mother is and they are investigating details of his disappearance . Difficult words: custody (care), nomadic (moving from one place to another), disappearance (going missing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A volcanic eruption rattled southwest Iceland, releasing lava and smoke following weeks of intense seismic activity. The eruption posed a threat to the town of Grindavik, leading authorities to evacuate nearly 4,000 residents last month and shut down the Blue Lagoon geothermal spa. The Meteorological Office issued warnings as the eruption started just kilometers from Grindavik, with a rapidly growing 3.5-kilometer crack in the earth’s surface. Keflavik International Airport experienced delays despite remaining open. The eruption is a result of the movement between tectonic plates in the Reykjanes peninsula and it’s generating significant lava flow and seismic activity, prompting heightened alert levels and public warnings to stay away. Difficult words: rattle (to cause to shake), geothermal (relating to or produced by the internal heat of the earth), seismic (relating to or caused by earthquakes). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Blue Lagoon spa closed last month, too. The eruption caused cracks in the ground and it extended towards the village. Keflavik International Airport remains open but there are delays. Difficult words: threat (possible danger), extend (to become wider or larger), release (to let move or flow freely). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A fox cub , presumably looking for food, got itself stuck in a dishwasher in a London household. Luckily for it, the owner found it and is a vet. With years of experience, he could tell that the fox was just a few months old and seemed to be very scared. He removed the dishwasher’s bottom trolley and, after some persuasion with a sweeping brush, the frightened animal crept out of the appliance and made a dash for the garden where people later saw it with its mother. Difficult words: cub (a baby animal such as a fox or a bear), presumably (probably, what somebody would think), persuasion (persuading somebody – telling him or her to do something), creep (move slowly and carefully), make a dash for (run somewhere suddenly and fast). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: trolley (a metal basket on wheels), sweeping brush (a brush on a stick, which people use to sweep – brush away dirt on the floor). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Heavy rain from former Tropical Cyclone Jasper has led to severe floods in Northeast Australia, isolating several towns. Queensland experienced record-breaking rain, causing widespread flash flooding . The flooding is described as the worst in memory by Premier Steven Miles. In Ingham, a town of 5,000, officials captured a crocodile in a storm drain. The Gateway town to the Great Barrier Reef, with over 150,000 residents, received triple the December average rainfall in 40 hours. More rain is forecasted, with major flood warnings issued. Thousands have evacuated, and power outages affect over 14,000 properties. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese mentioned Defense Forces are on standby for rescue efforts. Australia faces extreme weather, with the Northeast battling floods while the Southeast is on Bushfire alert. Difficult words: flash flood (a sudden local flood), power outage (loss of electric power in an area). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: flash flood (a sudden flood), average (usual), alert (being watchful of possible danger or problem). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A soldier is lucky to be alive after a 40-millimetre grenade accidentally fired from a grenade launcher and embedded itself in his face. The terrible accident happened in Colombia and surgeons had to be especially careful with the operation. The soldier could not be moved to hospital by helicopter due to the risk of the explosive detonating , so an ambulance transferred him in an eight-hour ride to Bogota. The team of doctors had to improvise and operate outside the hospital to minimise impact on the building in case the grenade exploded. Luckily, the operation was a success and the soldier could reintegrate into his military unit and his family to make a full recovery. Difficult words: embed (stuck into something), due to (because of), detonate (explode), improvise (make up how to do something), reintegrate (come back into a group). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Doctors operated on him outside of hospital for safety, too. The unusual operation was a success and the soldier is going to be fine. Difficult words: occur (happen), grenade launcher (a big gun which shoots things like grenades), stuck (if something is stuck somewhere, it gets in but cannot get out). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The world is transitioning to cleaner energy sources, creating a demand for critical metals used in everyday items like smartphones and electric vehicles. Recycling startup Nth Cycle is innovating metal refining technology to extract these metals efficiently and sustainably. They address the growing electronic waste issue, emphasizing the importance of clean energy technology starting with critical minerals such as cobalt, nickel, and manganese. Nth Cycle’s electro-extraction process reduces carbon emissions significantly compared to traditional methods. The startup aims to revolutionize metal refining with a modular and distributed approach that minimizes transportation costs and emissions. While facing challenges in an industry accustomed to traditional methods, Nth Cycle seeks to contribute to a sustainable world by refining critical minerals, the new essential resources for the clean energy economy. Difficult words: revolutionize (to change something radically), modular (consisting of independent units), refine (to make fine or pure). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The company has many problems because this industry uses traditional methods, but they believe that what they do is important for the clean energy economy. Difficult words: demand (when many companies or people want to buy something), extract (to take out), traditional (something what exists for a long time and doesn’t change much). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
